statement: You are given a singly linked list whose node values, read from head to tail, are listed in values. The tail's next pointer goes back to the node at 0-based position cycleIndex, so the list always contains a loop.
The algorithm sees only the head. Find the loop and count how many distinct nodes lie on it.
Return the number of nodes in the loop.

examples.explanation: The tail 6 links back to the node holding 3, so the loop is 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 3, which has 4 nodes.
The tail links back to the head, so every one of the 4 nodes is on the loop.
The tail 5 points to itself, so the loop holds a single node.
